ab.title: Crest orientation, bed-instability mode (αH)
ab.description: Crest orientation $\alpha_H$ of the bed-instability mode: the axis (0–180°) of crests that receive the largest gross sand transport across them, including the speed-up of the wind over the crest (Rubin & Hunter 1987; Courrech du Pont et al. 2024). It is also the expected crest orientation of migrating dunes such as barchans. Dunes with this orientation migrate perpendicular to it, in direction $\alpha_T$. As an axis it has no compass direction: e.g., 128° and 308° are the same line.

ae.title: Elongation direction (αE)
ae.description: Elongation direction $\alpha_E$: the direction in which a dune grows in length without migrating, where the net sand flux across its crest is zero and the net flux along it is positive (Courrech du Pont et al. 2014, 2024). It applies to dunes on beds with limited sand, typically growing from a fixed sand source. Where a wind regime allows several such directions, the atlas shows the most stable one.

at.title: Transverse migration direction (αT)
at.description: Migration direction $\alpha_T$ of dunes whose crests have the bed-instability orientation $\alpha_H$: perpendicular to $\alpha_H$, toward the side of the net sand flux across the crest (Gunn 2026; Courrech du Pont et al. 2024).

ao.title: Along-crest transport direction (αO)
ao.description: Direction $\alpha_O$ along crests of the bed-instability orientation $\alpha_H$ in which the net sand flux along the crest points, as a compass bearing. Where crests are oblique to the net transport, sand moves along them as well as across them; $\alpha_O$ shows which way along the crest it moves.

rdpa.title: Resultant drift direction (RDD)
rdpa.description: Direction of the time-averaged flat-bed flux vector, $\arg \sum n q e^{i\theta}$, the direction sand moves, as a compass bearing (clockwise from north). Poorly defined where RDP/DP is low, because transport in opposing directions nearly cancels.

dpm.title: Drift potential (DP)
dpm.description: Time-averaged flat-bed saturated sand flux, $DP = \sum n q / \sum n$ over all speed and direction bins: the volume of packed sand per metre width that the wind could move per year over a flat bed fully covered by loose sand (Gunn 2026). Like the drift potential of Fryberger & Dean (1979) it measures the wind's capacity to transport sand, but it is a different quantity: Fryberger's DP is in vector units, computed from 10 m wind speeds in knots as $V^2(V - V_t)$ with a 12-knot threshold, whereas this DP is a physical flux computed from the friction velocity with the threshold set by the slider. The two cannot be converted into each other without the wind-speed distribution, and Fryberger's energy classes (below 200, 200–400 and above 400 vector units) do not apply to these values.
dpm.descriptionMars: Time-averaged flat-bed saturated sand flux, $DP = \sum q / N$ over all N hours of the Mars year: the volume of packed sand per metre width that the wind could move per Earth year over a flat bed fully covered by loose sand (Gunn 2026). Like the drift potential of Fryberger & Dean (1979) it measures the wind's capacity to transport sand, but it is a different quantity: Fryberger's DP is in vector units, computed from 10 m wind speeds in knots as $V^2(V - V_t)$ with a 12-knot threshold, whereas this DP is a physical flux computed from the friction velocity with a threshold computed from the grain diameter. The two cannot be converted into each other, and Fryberger's energy classes do not apply to these values.

rdpm.title: Resultant drift potential (RDP)
rdpm.description: Magnitude of the time-averaged flat-bed flux vector, $RDP = |\sum n q e^{i\theta}| / \sum n$: the net volume of packed sand per metre width per year after transport in opposing directions has cancelled. Same units as DP; RDP ≤ DP, with equality only when all transport is in one direction.

qnlb.title: Net along-crest flux, bed-instability mode ⟨Q∥(αH)⟩
qnlb.titleTex: Net along-crest flux, bed-instability mode $\langle Q_{\parallel}(\alpha_H)\rangle$
qnlb.description: Net along-crest bed-instability-mode flux $\langle Q_{\parallel}(\alpha_H)\rangle$ in m$^2$/s.

qncb.title: Net across-crest flux, bed-instability mode ⟨Q⊥(αH)⟩
qncb.titleTex: Net across-crest flux, bed-instability mode $\langle Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)\rangle$
qncb.description: Net across-crest bed-instability-mode flux $\langle Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)\rangle$ in m$^2$/s.

qalb.title: Absolute along-crest flux, bed-instability mode ⟨|Q∥(αH)|⟩
qalb.description: Absolute along-crest bed-instability-mode flux $\langle |Q_{\parallel}(\alpha_H)|\rangle$ in m$^2$/s.

qacb.title: Absolute across-crest flux, bed-instability mode ⟨|Q⊥(αH)|⟩
qacb.description: Absolute across-crest bed-instability-mode flux $\langle |Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)|\rangle$ in m$^2$/s.

qnle.title: Net along-crest flux, elongation mode ⟨Q∥(αE)⟩
qnle.titleTex: Net along-crest flux, elongation mode $\langle Q_{\parallel}(\alpha_E)\rangle$

qha_rdp_dp.title: Flux directionality (RDP/DP)
qha_rdp_dp.description: Directional variability of sand flux: ratio of resultant to total drift potential, $RDP/DP$ (0 = multidirectional, 1 = unidirectional). Undefined where there is no sand flux ($DP = 0$). Fryberger & Dean (1979) classes: below 0.3 low (complex or obtuse bimodal winds), 0.3–0.8 intermediate (obtuse to acute bimodal winds), above 0.8 high (unimodal winds). Only transport above the threshold counts here, and the flux law differs from Fryberger's, so use the classes as a guide.

sige_sigh.title: Stability of elongating dunes on starved beds (σE/σH)
sige_sigh.titleTex: Stability of elongating dunes on starved beds $\sigma_E/\sigma_H$
sige_sigh.description: Ratio of the growth rates in height of dunes in the elongation and bed-instability orientations, $\langle|Q_{\bot}(\alpha_E)|\rangle/\langle|Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)|\rangle$, between 0 and 1. It assesses whether dunes elongating from a sand source on a starved bed are stable: in numerical simulations and in dunes around the Tibesti Massif, elongating linear dunes form where the ratio is above about 0.6 and trains of barchans form below it (Gao et al. 2015; Courrech du Pont et al. 2024). It does not take bed mobility or other boundary conditions into account.

qhab_nl_nc.title: Crest straightness vs sinuosity, bed-instability mode (Q̂∥/⊥,H)
qhab_nl_nc.titleTex: Crest straightness vs sinuosity, bed-instability mode $\hat{Q}_{\parallel/\bot,H}$
qhab_nl_nc.description: Net along-crest over net across-crest sand flux for crests of the bed-instability orientation, $|\langle Q_{\parallel}(\alpha_H)\rangle/\langle Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)\rangle|$. Along-crest transport tends to keep crests straight, while across-crest transport, which drives migration, tends to make them sinuous (Rubin 2012), so higher values suggest straighter long-crested dunes on sand-covered beds. For dunes migrating on starved beds, the ratio measures the asymmetry of sand fluxes that makes dunes such as barchans asymmetric (Courrech du Pont et al. 2024). In the sand-covered-bed examples of Courrech du Pont et al. (2024) it is about 0.03 for transverse, 0.4 for oblique and 22 for longitudinal dunes. The ratio goes to infinity where its denominator (a net flux) goes to zero (shown clipped to ±60,000).

qhab_ac_nc.title: Growth-in-height vs migration balance (Q̂|⊥|/⊥,H)
qhab_ac_nc.description: Gross over net across-crest sand flux for crests of the bed-instability orientation, $|\langle |Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)|\rangle/\langle Q_{\bot}(\alpha_H)\rangle|$, never below 1: the balance between growth in height and migration. Values near 1 mean that transport across the crest goes one way and the dunes mainly migrate; large values mean that it reverses, building the dunes up with little net migration, which may also favour straighter crests (Courrech du Pont et al. 2024). In the sand-covered-bed examples of Courrech du Pont et al. (2024) it is about 1.1 for transverse, 5 for oblique and 49 for longitudinal dunes. The ratio goes to infinity where its denominator (a net flux) goes to zero (shown clipped to ±60,000).

qhne_ac_nl.title: Morphology of elongating dunes (Q̂|⊥|/∥,E)
qhne_ac_nl.description: Gross across-crest over net along-crest sand flux for dunes in the elongation orientation, $\langle |Q_{\bot}(\alpha_E)|\rangle/\langle Q_{\parallel}(\alpha_E)\rangle$: the balance between growth in height and elongation. For dunes that elongate without migrating, it is the parameter expected to distinguish their shapes. Compared with $\hat{Q}_{|\bot|/\bot,H}$, it indicates whether elongation or migration is more likely to set dune shape and orientation on a starved bed: the dynamic with the larger ratio favours growth in height more and is expected to prevail (Courrech du Pont et al. 2024). The ratio goes to infinity where its denominator (a net flux) goes to zero (shown clipped to ±60,000).

ufm.title: Mean above-threshold friction velocity / threshold (⟨u*f | u*f > u*th⟩ / u*th)
ufm.descriptionMars: Average above-threshold flat-bed friction velocity, normalised by threshold $\langle u_{\ast,f}|u_{\ast,f}>u_{\ast,th}\rangle/u_{\ast,th}$. The threshold is that hour's cessation threshold $u_{\ast,th}(d, \rho_f, T)$ of Pähtz & Durán (2023).

uft.title: Fraction of time above threshold (T | u*f > u*th / T)
uft.descriptionMars: Fraction of time flat-bed friction velocity is above threshold $T|u_{\ast,f}>u_{\ast,th}/T$. The threshold is that hour's cessation threshold $u_{\ast,th}(d, \rho_f, T)$ of Pähtz & Durán (2023).

qhbf.title: Fraction of bed-instability-mode flux while flat bed above threshold
qhbf.titleTex: Fraction of bed-instability-mode flux while flat bed above threshold
qhbf.description: Fraction of bed-instability-mode ($\alpha_H$) crest flux that occurs while the flat-bed friction velocity exceeds threshold, $\sum_{u_{\ast,f}>u_{\ast,th}} n|Q(\alpha_H)| / \sum n|Q(\alpha_H)|$. 0 where crest flux occurs only while the flat bed is below threshold; undefined where there is no crest flux.
qhbf.descriptionMars: Fraction of bed-instability-mode ($\alpha_H$) crest flux that occurs while the flat-bed friction velocity exceeds threshold, $\sum_{u_{\ast,f}>u_{\ast,th}} n|Q(\alpha_H)| / \sum n|Q(\alpha_H)|$. 0 where crest flux occurs only while the flat bed is below threshold; undefined where there is no crest flux. The threshold is that hour's cessation threshold $u_{\ast,th}(d, \rho_f, T)$ of Pähtz & Durán (2023).

qhef.title: Fraction of elongation-mode flux while flat bed above threshold
qhef.titleTex: Fraction of elongation-mode flux while flat bed above threshold
qhef.descriptionMars: Fraction of elongation-mode ($\alpha_E$) crest flux that occurs while the flat-bed friction velocity exceeds threshold, $\sum_{u_{\ast,f}>u_{\ast,th}} n|Q(\alpha_E)| / \sum n|Q(\alpha_E)|$. 0 where crest flux occurs only while the flat bed is below threshold; undefined where there is no crest flux. The threshold is that hour's cessation threshold $u_{\ast,th}(d, \rho_f, T)$ of Pähtz & Durán (2023).
